Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

excuse noun and verb

a reason given to explain a fault

also make excuses, make my excuses, an excuse, pretext, no excuse, excuse oneself

classical

Cic. Fam. 4.4.1: accipiō excūsātiōnem tuam
Cic. Att. 12.29.1: quaerenda erit excūsātiō ad Brūtum
Traupman 311

excūsātiō, excūsātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an excuse

Often with a genitive of the ground pleaded, excūsātiō aetātis, valētūdinis, the excuse of age, of health (Lewis & Short). Excūsātiōnem accipere, to accept an excuse.

Other words

  • excūsō, excūsāre, excūsāvī, excūsātum — excuse; make (someone’s) excuses; plead as an excuse

    verb, first conjugation; aliquem alicui, mē (tibi) excūsō · classical · Cic. Att. 15.28: Atticae meae velim mē ita excūsēs ut omnem culpam in tē trānsferās; Cic. Q. Fr. 2.2.1 (Lewis & Short): prīmum mē tibi excūsō in eō ipsō, in quō tē accūsō; Traupman 311

    To clear of blame, the opposite of accūsāre: mē tibi excūsō, I apologise (see I apologise); ut excūser morbī causā, that I be excused on grounds of illness (Cic. Att. 12.13.2). For “excuse me” and forgiving a fault, see excuse me, forgive.

  • causa, causae f. — a pretext, an excuse

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 138: fingit causās nē det sēdulō

    The general word for a cause or reason; it is also a feigned reason, a pretext: causās fingere, to make up excuses; per causam, on the pretext of (Lewis & Short). Its everyday senses are a reason and a lawsuit (see reason).

  • praetextum, praetextī n. — pretext

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 311; Suet. Caes. 30: et praetextum quidem illī cīvīlium armōrum hoc fuit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 364

    Post-Augustan in this sense (Lewis & Short); Cicero says speciēs or simulātiō.

Examples

  • Atticae meae velim mē ita excūsēs ut omnem culpam in tē trānsferās

    please make my excuses to my little Attica, and put all the blame on yourselfCic. Att. 15.28

  • postquam sēnsit mē tēcum quoque rem habēre, fingit causās nē det sēdulō.

    once he realised I was seeing you too, he kept making up excuses not to hand her over.Ter. Eun. 137–138

  • sed in hōc homine nūllam accipiō excūsātiōnem.

    But in this man’s case I accept no excuse.Cic. Fam. 2.14.1

  • praetextum bellī

    a pretext for warTraupman 364

  • Hinc abiit quasi…

    He left under the pretext that…Traupman 364

See also excuse me, I apologise, forgive, I’m sorry, reason.
